content: The foolish man who comes among others does best to hold his tongue; no one will discover how little he knows unless he speaks too much.
author: Celtic & Norse Proverbs
sourceWork: Ósnotr maðr er með aldir kemr (Hávamál, Stanza 27) — Poetic Edda
explanation: A fool feels an insecure urge to fill every quiet pause with chatter, eagerly broadcasting their ignorance to the entire hall. The disciplined individual knows that silence is a sanctuary of observation: in quietness you learn the lay of the land, understand the motives of others, and preserve your dignity.
practicalInsight: Practice intentional silence in conversations today. Listen twice as much as you speak.
reflectionPrompt: Do you speak out of genuine insight, or merely to assure yourself and others that you take up space?
